cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Make the Test Test You
cards.instruction: Create a commitment test that gradually exposes what you are unwilling to risk yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed my name on the night rota like you. Take the midnight shift if this shelter matters to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My cross cancels my shift. You just cancelled yours too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, clearing space to supervise. You take midnight to four and I'll stay available.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll do it if you sit at the desk beside me. We can split the calls.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could we split them before midnight? I need to be asleep by eleven to supervise properly.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies crossing a name without knowing it cancels duty and tests B's commitment; A3 pretends supervisory availability; A5 reveals its sleep limit when B4 asks reciprocal labor.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cancellation causes A3 supervisory cover; B4 splitting calls causes A5 request to split them before the shift even starts.

relationship.evidence: B4 offers an equal workload and a concrete desk role.

heightening.evidence: A5 exposes exactly what A will not risk—sleep—while still performing managerial certainty.

specificity.evidence: A1 shelter/night rota and A3 midnight-four plus A5 eleven bedtime make the contradiction plainly character-level.
